implementation_notes: C has no interfaces, so the pattern survives literally: each extension interface is a struct of function pointers plus an identifier (string, GUID or GType), the subject carries a table of extensions and one query entry point such as void *query_interface(subject *, const char *id) that returns NULL when the extension is absent, and adapters are installed by an external register function because a C type cannot gain a method at run time. Identifier discipline is the hard part: strings need one registry that guarantees uniqueness, and every call site must NULL-check before dereferencing the table, since there is no RTTI to catch a mistaken answer. In glib-based code prefer the GObject variant - the type system owns the registry and the query becomes g_type_interface_peek.
pitfalls: query_interface returns void *: every call site needs an explicit NULL check before touching the function pointers, and a mistyped id silently yields NULL.
Identifier uniqueness is manual (strings or GUIDs); duplicate ids collide at run time with no compiler help.
Extension tables and adapter objects are unmanaged memory - the subject must own and free them or every query leaks.
Function-pointer tables carry no RTTI, so nothing verifies that an object really implements the interface it answers for.

variants.name: GObject interface conformances (glib type system)
variants.implementation_notes: With glib present the registry is the type system: declare the extension contract with G_DEFINE_INTERFACE, implement it per class with G_IMPLEMENT_INTERFACE inside G_DEFINE_TYPE_WITH_CODE, and ask at run time with g_type_interface_peek(klass, iface_type), which returns NULL when the class does not conform - the same total query, now library-supplied. Cost: the interface structure is a vtable shared by all instances of a class, so per-instance state must live on the instance or in data attached through the interface init function.
variants.code_sketch:
G_DEFINE_INTERFACE (TextAccessor, text_accessor, G_TYPE_OBJECT)
G_DEFINE_TYPE_WITH_CODE (Component, component, G_TYPE_OBJECT,
                         G_IMPLEMENT_INTERFACE (TEXT_ACCESSOR_TYPE,
                                                component_text_accessor_init))

TextAccessor *ta = g_type_interface_peek (G_OBJECT_GET_CLASS (component),
                                          TEXT_ACCESSOR_TYPE);
if (ta) text_accessor_word_count (component);
pitfalls: g_type_interface_peek returns the vtable shared by every instance of the class - never store per-instance state there.
The interface init function runs once per implementing class; leaving function pointers unset (or skipping the default-init guard) aborts at call time.
Interface conformance is fixed when the GType is registered, so you cannot add a conformance to an existing class at run time.
